title.narrative: KEWASNET Förbättrad styrning i kenyanska vattensektorn, Fas 2

description.narrative:
Kenya Water and Sanitation Civil Society Network (KEWASNET)(Nätverksorganisationen för Kenyas Civilsamhällesorganisationer i Vattensektorn) är det nationella nätverket för ett antal (för närvarande 77) civilsamhällesorganisationer i vattensektorn i Kenya. Sveriges Ambassad i Nairobi (härefter EoS) har stött KEWASNET att genomföra ett Program för Förbättrad Styrning i Vattensektorn (Water Governance Support Programme) (härefter WGSP I) under åren 2014 - 2019. EoS emottog ett förslag från KEWASNET för en andra fas av programmet, WGSP II, med en slutlig förhandlad budget om 23 MSEK som gåvostöd i form av program-stöd, innehållande resultat-baserad outsourcing/ vidareförmedling av upp til ca 20% av programbudgeten till medlemsorganisationer, med start i november 2019. En förlängning med budgettillskott av avtalet för WGSP I för att täcka övergångsaktiviteter under juli - oktober 2019 har också genomförts.
WGSP II kommer att fördjupa och kopiera framgångsrika aktiviteter från WGSP I (många av dessa är process-orienterade och tar tid att genomföra), men också identifiera nya öppningar i vattensektorn och ta sig an nya tematiker och geografiska områden. Arbetssättet kommer att vara agilt och adaptivt för att hålla takten med utvecklingen i sektorn..
WGSP II har som mål att verka för hållbar förvaltning av vattenresurser och förbättrad WASH (vattenförsörjning, sanitet och hygien) i Kenya, med fokus på de mest eftersatta i befolkningen. Genom aktiviteter som genomförs av KEWASNETs sekretariat och medlemsorganisationer, med rättighetsbaserade arbetsmetoder, så kommer programmet att från ett civilsamhällesperspektiv stärka WASH- och vattenresursförvaltningsinstitutioner och intressenter, styrningsmekanismer och regelsefterlevnad inom urban sanitet, styrningsmekanismer och modeller för utbyggnad av vatten och sanitet på landsbygden, sektorkoordinering, ansvarsutkrävande, folkets röst, kapacitet hos civilsamhällesorganisationer, och medborgarinflytande i centrala policyprocesser.
Programmet kommer att genomföras på länsnivå, regional nivå, nationell nivå och internationell nivå, med fokus på 10 län främst i centrala och södra/västra Kenya (Kwale, Tharaka-Nithi, Machakos, Makueni, Baringo, Laikipia, Narok, Kakamega, Busia, Nyamira).
Medan WGSP II tematiskt bygger på och skalar upp WGSP I, så föreslår EoS att inte operationellt länka ihop de två avtalen genom konditionalitet för utbetalningar etc. Återbetalning av medel från WGSP I (eventuella rapporterade oanvända medel, utestående förväntade återbetalade WGSP I - medel från Chase Bank-kollapsen 2016 (ca 500 000 SEK) , och möjlig avskrivning av den förlust av ca 500 000 SEK som också gjordes vid Chase Bank--kollapsen, kommer att hanteras separat under en förlängning av WGSP I-avtalet.

The Kenya Water and Sanitation Civil Society Network (KEWASNET) is the national network of (currently 77) water civil society organisations in Kenya. The Embassy of Sweden in Nairobi (EoS hereafter) has supported KEWASNET to implement a Water Governance Support Programme (hereafter WGSP I) during the years 2014 - 2019. EoS received a proposal from KEWASNET for a second phase of the programme, Water Governance Support Programme II, with a final negotiated budget of 23 MSEK as grant programme support over 3 years , including results-based outsourcing/ ongranting of up to around 20% of the budget to member organisations, to start in November 2019. A cost extension of WGSP I covering transition activities in July - October 2019 has also been undertaken.
The Water Governance Support Programme II will deepen and replicate successful activities from WGSP I (many are process-oriented which take time), but also seize new opportunities in the sector and venture into new thematic and geographical areas. The approach will be agile and adaptive to keep up with new developments in the sector.
The WGSP II aims to promote Sustainable Management of Water Resources and Improved WASH (Water, Sanitation and Hygiene) services in Kenya, with a focus on Leaving No-one Behind. Through activities undertaken by its Secretariat and member organisations, using human rights based approaches, the programme will from a CSO perspective strengthen WASH- and WRM institutions and stakeholders, urban sanitation regulatory and compliance environment, rural water and sanitation services provision and regulation, sector coordination, accountability mechanisms, citizens' voice, capacity of CSOs, and public participation in key policy development processes.
The programme will intevene at sub-national/county, regional, national and international levels, with a focus on 10 counties mainly in central and Southern/ Western Kenya (Kwale, Tharaka-Nithi, Machakos, Makueni, Baringo, Laikipia, Narok, Kakamega, Busia, Nyamira).
While the WGSP II thematically builds on and scales out WGSP I, EoS proposes not to link the two agreements operationally through conditions for disbursements etc. Repayment of funds due from WGSP I (any eventual balances, outstanding expected repayments of WGSP I funds from the 2016 Chase Bank collapse amounting to approximately 500 000 SEK, and possible write-off of losses incurred from the same 2016 Chase Bank collapse amounting to approximately 500 000 SEK) will be handled separately under an extension of the WGSP I agreement.

The Water Governance Support Programme II aims to promote Sustainable Management of Water Resources and Improved WASH (Water, Sanitation and Hygiene) services in Kenya. The programme will be anchored on four outcome areas including:
Outcome 1: Improved management of water resources, and water and sanitation services provision Outcome 2: Improved coordination of sector interventions Outcome 3: Improved transparency, integrity, accountability and sector decision making Outcome 4: Strong and active institutions that effectively respond to the SDG ambition.

title.narrative: Decision KEWASNET Förbättrad Styrning i Kenyanska Vattensektorn

description.narrative:
Results examples Progress during 2021 was good given the circumstances of the continued Covid-19 pandemic. KEWASNET adopted a different strategy to engage implementing partners who implemented the programme in 2021. Amid the Covid-19 turbulence, most implementing partners planned the activities and involved the right stakeholders in a timely manner. This led to strong partnerships and teamwork which enhanced effectiveness in program execution.
Outcome 1: Improved management of Water Resources, and Water and Sanitation Services provision During the last year, KEWASNET focused on the dissemination of the various studies including mapping of WRM capacities, on site sanitation mapping, learnings and evidence from CLTS Implementation. These were mainly done at the various workshops that brought together stakeholders in the sector. The reports were disseminated mainly through virtual and social platforms apart from anchoring them on the website for KEWASNET. Through the dissemination, it is envisaged that the knowledge gaps as identified in the sector will be filled, and above all create synergies and collaboration resulting to improved management of water resources and service provision. The Technical Working Groups focusing on Leave no one behind were conducted by KWAHO in collaboration with other KEWASNET partners in targeted counties from Mt. Kenya region in Embu and particularly, Tharaka Nithi and Laikipia counties. Stakeholders were drawn from CSOs, private and social enterprises with interest in the WASH/WRM sector, government and academia. Some of the key conclusions that were drawn during the discussions include; LNOB is a critical subject, and its crosscutting nature calls for a multi-stakeholder and multi-sectoral approach.
To support and improve water service provision among the consumers in Kenya, most water companies who participated in KEWASNET WASH forums which have significantly impacted their operations by giving them a better understanding of customer needs. For instance, Busia Water and Sanitation Company Limited (BUWASCO) provides water and sanitation services to the residents of Busia at a subsidized fee. They offer services at a subsidized fee within 7 schemes, Mundika, Malakisi, Matayos, Malakisi, Nambale, Bujumba, and Bumala, serving 110,000 residents through at least 10,000 connections. The BUWASCO managing director, Mr Erick Ojiambo says: "Initially, there was a common understanding that water is for free, hence, service providers should be giving it for free. Such a belief created a negative attitude towards among consumers to BUWASCO. However, through WASH forums facilitated by KEWASNET, we got opportunities to explain in detail the operations of the company and how residents could support it. For example, the water we get from River Sio is brown, it needs to be treated, pumped from the intake, and pumped from the tank. All this is a cost. Thus, it is important for the customers understand that the little payment they provide is important. Also, KEWASNET has positively impacted BUWASCO through understanding the value of partnership for the benefit of the community. And that is why as BUWASCO, we committed to provide water to the newly launched hand-washing stations in Busia to promote hand hygiene to minimize the spread of Covid-19 at the border point."
Outcome 2: Improved coordination of sector interventions During the period, most of the forums were run through the virtual meetings especially those that targeted national events while those at the county level had limited attendances. Due to the nature of coordination function in Kenya, many intended forums did not take place, however a there was a deliberate focus on county WASH forums during the second half of 2021 which resulted to improved coordination of the sector. To promote coordination in information gathering and management, KEWASNET collected human interest stories on marginalized communities and types of vulnerabilities in target counties of Baringo, Busia and Kakamega counties for WGSP II programme. The focus was to ensure that the vulnerable and marginalized have a space to participate and make decisions in the sector thus creating partnerships which promotes the Leave No One Behind principles. This outcome was largely supported by the new approach that KEWASNET adopted of conducting virtual meetings from the previous year. And with it, KEWASNET was able to increase the number of participants.
Outcome 3: Improved transparency, integrity, accountability and sector decision making in WASH and WRM KEWASNET developed and disseminated the 7th edition of the CSO Annual Water and Sanitation Sector Performance Report 2019-20; the VOICE. The report has been utilized as a sector accountability tool to foster cross learning among Government, CSOs, private sector and enterprises not only on program effectiveness and efficiency but also embrace sustainability and innovative approaches in the sector. A total of 205 CSOs participated in the survey which depicted tremendous commitment of the civil society towards open and transparent engagement on their contributions to the WASH and WRM sectors.
Outcome 4: Strong and active institutions that effectively respond to the SDG ambition One of the achievements for KEWASNET in 2021 was the ability to conduct TWGs and study cycles which not only brought key stakeholders together but also forged to attain necessary solutions to some of the far-reaching challenges in the WASH/WRM sector. KEWASNET conducted the study cycles which targeted Nyamira and Laikipia reaching out to various stakeholders in the two counties. The overall aim of the study cycles was to induct sector actors on key orientations around SDG 6 and define key priorities for building momentum.
High Level/Institutional/Sector Level Achievements and Impacts The launch of the Annual CSO report in the sector dubbed the Voice has continuously attracted the attention of the key actors both at national level and regionally both as critical reference and for decision making. The report has also be able to highlight key thematic areas implemented and milestones made in the sector, as a way to influence future programming. The findings from the technical working groups conducted by KEWASNET for the WASH/WRM sector reveals that amid progress made on the implementation of the Water Act 2016, there are still pending institutional issues that need amendments. This includes the realignment of the Water Act 2016 with national policies to enlighten roles and mandates of key sector institutions, while at the same time, addressing other components like water sector financing especially among WRUAs and rural based water service provision side-lined by most county governments. The marketplace exhibitions organized by KEWASNET, its implementing partners and other like-minded organizations in Kisumu where more than 75 participants showcased different innovations in the sector created not only a platform to strengthen networking and partnerships, but also a hub to exchange new ideas and knowledge products. Specifically, the market place sought to create a forum for exchange of knowledge/ information; create space for networking; promote the work of CSOs and celebrate different sector players and the innovations they bring to the table. One of the key lessons learnt in the event is the need to scale up WASH and WRM innovations.
